https://www.mediafax.ro/english/nicusor-.text: Nicușor Dan heads to the UN General Assembly. Speech in New York and lobbying for Dacian Cioloș President Nicușor Dan will lead Romania’s delegation to the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, according to information released Friday by the Presidential Administration. On September 23, the head of state will deliver Romania’s national statement in the General Assembly plenary during the high-level segment, which is attended annually by leaders from around the world. The 81st session of the General Assembly officially opens on September 8, 2026, and the high-level general debate is scheduled for September 22–28, with a break on September 27. The UN has confirmed that this year’s meeting will be held under the theme “Restoring Trust, Managing Transformation: A United Nations That Delivers Results for All.” According to the Presidential Administration, the president’s speech will focus on reforming the United Nations, as well as on Romania’s contribution to ensuring international peace and security. Nicușor Dan is set to reaffirm Romania’s support for an international order based on rules and norms, in a context marked by Russia’s war against Ukraine and other international conflicts and crises. UN reform will, in fact, be one of the key topics of the session. The president-elect of the 81st session of the General Assembly, Bangladeshi diplomat Khalilur Rahman, has identified peace and security, climate change, human rights, emerging technologies, and UN reform as among his priorities. The General Assembly brings together all 193 UN member states, each with one vote. Unlike the Security Council, General Assembly resolutions are generally not legally binding, but the assembly remains one of the main global diplomatic forums. The visit to New York will also have an important diplomatic component for Romania. On the sidelines of the meeting, Nicușor Dan will participate in several events and hold bilateral meetings with heads of state and government. Among the topics promoted by the Romanian side will be Romania’s candidacy for the leadership of the International Organization of La Francophonie (OIF). The candidate supported by Romania is Dacian Cioloș, a former prime minister and former European Commissioner for Agriculture. Nicușor Dan officially announced his candidacy in March 2026. At stake is the election of the future Secretary General of the Francophonie for the 2027–2030 term, a decision to be made by the heads of state and government at the Francophonie Summit scheduled for November 2026 in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. The OIF announced that four candidates have entered the race, from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Mauritania, Romania, and Rwanda. The candidates were interviewed for the first time as part of a formal procedure in Paris at the end of June. Cioloș was also appointed presidential advisor in April, explaining at the time that the position allows him to lead the international campaign for the OIF presidency and to act on behalf of the president in this matter. This year’s attendance contrasts with the decision made by Nicușor Dan in September 2025, when he did not personally attend the UN General Assembly. Romania was represented at that time by Foreign Minister Oana Țoiu, who delivered the national address in the plenary session. Official UN records confirm that the head of Romanian diplomacy represented Romania at the general debate of the 80th session. When asked later why he did not travel to New York, Nicușor Dan explained that he had made a “cost-benefit analysis” and that he considered it “more useful to be present in the country,” citing political meetings, discussions with investors, a CSAT meeting, and the review of legislative acts. In 2026, however, the president will personally attend the meeting in New York and lead the Romanian delegation. The Presidential Administration notes that the visit’s agenda is still being finalized, and the complete list of bilateral meetings and events in which Nicușor Dan will participate will be announced closer to the General Assembly. https://www.thenationalnews.com/news/eur.text: Ukraine is ready to agree to a deal with Russia to halt attacks on each other’s energy supplies, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said. Mr Zelenskyy was responding to US President Donald Trump’s announcement that there would be an “energy ceasefire” between Russia and Ukraine. Speaking by video at the Warsaw Security Conference, the Ukrainian leader said he learnt about the proposed truce from the media, after Mr Trump made the announcement on his Truth Social platform on Sunday. “If the Americans need it, we are ready to sign these guarantees to make sure they can be trusted. It’s important that we all see this situation in the same way,” Mr Zelenskyy said. But he said Russian President Vladimir Putin “doesn’t read Truth Social” and that Ukraine continued to come under attack. Mr Zelenskyy added that “if Russia doesn’t agree to energy ceasefire, we will respond”. He urged Washington to step in to ensure that Moscow abided by the terms of the putative agreement. "There were ​Russian ⁠violations ‌of the energy ceasefire announced ​by President Trump," he said. "We are waiting for the details of the conditions between the Americans and Russians, and we are waiting to see one specific step the Americans are ready to take. "This energy ceasefire, it ⁠can work, and it can ⁠become a major step towards ending the war, if the Americans truly step in now and ​make sure Russians respect it." As Mr Trump made his announcement, large parts of Kyiv were without electricity and water as repair crews struggled to restore power after Russian strikes. A power plant in Kharkiv, in the north-east, also came under attack. “All morning today, more and more Russian jet-powered Shaheds have continued to enter our skies over Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities,” said Mr Zelenskyy, referring to Iranian-supplied drones used by Russia in the war. “We shoot down many of them and, if we didn’t, there would clearly be even more damage to our energy infrastructure.” Mr Zelenskyy ended his address by urging Ukraine's allies to dedicate their time to making sure the US gets "one clear message". "An energy ceasefire and other steps to reduce escalation and guarantee security are truly needed here – in reality, not just on Truth Social,” he said. “We need to end Russia's war. We need to guarantee security. We need to stand together, Europe and the United States." At the weekend, Mr Zelenskyy held talks with key allies, including UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte. French President ​Emmanuel Macron ​said ​on Monday that ⁠he had not ⁠seen any ​signs in the past ⁠48 hours of Russia respecting an energy ceasefire. "We can only reopen the debate on ​the energy ‌situation if there ⁠is real ​ceasefire which is ​respected ‌by both sides," Mr Macron said at the Paris ⁠Autoshow. "I have not noted, over the last 48 hours, any energy ceasefire coming from ​the Russian side." Mr Burnham told Mr Zelenskyy that he recognised "the past 24 hours had been difficult for Ukraine” and stressed his “complete solidarity” with Kyiv, according to a Downing Street readout of the call between the two leaders. The pair discussed the “importance of maintaining pressure on Russia” and Mr Burnham made it clear that the UK “would continue to strengthen its sanctions on Russia and take further action to constrain the Russian war machine”. Mr Carney’s office said he had spoken with Mr Zelenskyy about Mr Trump’s “diesel deal” with Russia, which aims to immediately release 300,000 tonnes of the fuel to global markets in an effort to curb rising costs. The Canadian leader said the agreement was in "direct opposition to the efforts of Ukraine, Canada and our allies to create peace and stability in Europe". Mr Zelenskyy has proposed a 60-day ceasefire to allow his country to hold presidential elections, but that was immediately rejected by Russia. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said his country wanted a long-term peace deal rather than a temporary ceasefire.
